scope.q: What specific criteria or metrics currently define a 'ticket that matters' from the perspective of the business (e.g., churn risk, revenue impact, regulatory compliance, product severity)?
scope.why: Understanding the precise definition of 'matters' is fundamental to building an effective prioritization model and ensuring alignment with business goals.

scope.q: Which existing ticketing systems, communication channels (e.g., email, chat, phone transcripts), and data formats will need to be integrated for ticket ingestion?
scope.why: Identifying all input sources and their specific data structures is critical for designing the data ingestion and normalization pipeline accurately.

scope.q: What is the desired immediate action or insight an agent should receive for a 'ticket that matters' directly within their current workflow, and what level of automation is acceptable?
scope.why: This clarifies the expected output, the primary user interface, and the direct impact on the agent, guiding the design of the system's interaction points.

decomposition.title: Ticket Data Ingestion & Normalization
decomposition.why: To standardize diverse ticket data from various sources into a consistent, machine-readable format for downstream processing.

decomposition.title: LLM-Based Ticket Analysis & Categorization
decomposition.why: To extract key information, intent, sentiment, and classify tickets into relevant categories using advanced language models.

decomposition.title: Prioritization & Routing Engine
decomposition.why: To apply business rules and AI insights to rank tickets by urgency/importance and suggest optimal routing or agent actions.

decomposition.title: Agent Workspace Integration & UI
decomposition.why: To present prioritized tickets and AI-generated insights directly within the agents' existing tools or a dedicated interface, minimizing workflow disruption.

decomposition.title: Agent Feedback & Model Retraining Loop
decomposition.why: To capture agent corrections and feedback on classifications and priorities, enabling continuous improvement and adaptation of the underlying AI models.

decomposition.title: Performance Monitoring & Analytics
decomposition.why: To provide dashboards and reports on system effectiveness, ticket trends, agent performance, and 'ticket that matters' metrics for management.

components.name: External Ticketing System(s)
components.sub: Existing systems like Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, email.

components.name: Ticket Ingestion Service
components.sub: Pulls/receives raw ticket data, normalizes format.

components.name: Normalized Ticket Data Store
components.sub: Stores all ingested, normalized, and analyzed ticket data.

components.name: LLM Analysis Agent
components.sub: Processes ticket text for categorization, sentiment, intent, keywords.

components.name: Prioritization & Routing Service
components.sub: Applies business rules and LLM insights to rank tickets.

components.name: Agent Workspace UI
components.sub: Displays prioritized tickets and AI insights to support agents.

components.name: Agent Feedback Service
components.sub: Captures agent corrections and explicit feedback for model improvement.

components.name: Performance Metrics & Audit Log
components.sub: Stores system performance, model predictions, and agent feedback.

components.name: Analytics Dashboard
components.sub: Visualizes system performance, ticket trends, and 'mattering' metrics.

sprint.title: Core Infrastructure Setup & Ingestion MVP
sprint.deliv: Dockerized ingestion service deployed, successfully ingesting 100 sample tickets into a local database.

sprint.title: LLM-Based Initial Categorization PoC
sprint.deliv: Proof-of-concept LLM agent processes 50 sample tickets, categorizing them into 3 predefined, high-level categories.

sprint.title: Basic Prioritization & Agent UI (Read-Only)
sprint.deliv: Web UI displays 20 prioritized tickets with LLM analysis, fetched directly from the database, for agent review.

sprint.title: Read-Only Integration with Customer's Ticketing System
sprint.deliv: System successfully fetches actual tickets from customer's live ticketing system and displays them in the Agent UI.

sprint.title: Agent Feedback Loop Implementation
sprint.deliv: Agents can mark a ticket's priority or category as 'correct' or 'incorrect' in the UI, logging feedback to the system.

sprint.title: Performance Monitoring & Basic Dashboard
sprint.deliv: Dashboard displays key metrics like number of tickets processed, categorization accuracy (based on feedback), and top categories.

sprint.title: System Refinement, Testing, & Deployment Prep
sprint.deliv: System tested with 500 real tickets, all components integrated, and deployment scripts ready for a staging environment release.

risks.risk: Ambiguous or constantly changing definition of 'ticket that matters' leads to inconsistent or inaccurate LLM prioritization.
risks.mitigation: Establish a clear, documented process for defining and updating prioritization rules, incorporating regular stakeholder reviews and agent feedback sessions.

risks.risk: Poor quality, inconsistent formatting, or highly unstructured ticket data from existing systems results in inaccurate LLM analysis.
risks.mitigation: Develop robust data cleaning and normalization pipelines, and work with the customer to identify and address primary data quality issues at the source systems.

risks.risk: Low agent adoption due to perceived workflow disruption, lack of trust in AI-generated insights, or a cumbersome user experience.
risks.mitigation: Design the agent UI for minimal disruption, provide clear explanations for AI suggestions, and actively involve agents in early design and feedback iterations.

risks.risk: LLM model drift over time as customer issues, product features, or support language evolve, degrading model performance and relevance.
risks.mitigation: Implement a regular model retraining schedule using recent, agent-validated data, and establish continuous monitoring of key model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall).
